<pasted_content id="72da">
Build a new buyer agent for the Tacto Negotiation Arena from the spec in
negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md, on a new branch.

## Setup
1. Start from `feature/meso-agent`. The requirements file is untracked there, so commit it first
   ("docs: new agent requirements"). Then create `feature/spec-agent` from that commit and push it
   with upstream.
2. Read the whole requirements file before you write any code. Section 0 describes the case JSON the
   agent receives; treat it as the input contract. Then read `brief/api.md` (the rules, the cost
   formula C and the score) and the starter kit's README.md.

## Where the source code is
- Sections 1-10: BuyerAgent on `feature/team-agent`: arena_kit/agents/buyer.py, strategy.py,
  dossier.py
- Section 11: DualAgent on `feature/team-agent`: arena_kit/agents/dual.py, intel.py, tactics.py
- Section 12: TeamAgent on `feature/team-agent`: team/agent.py, levers.py, briefing.py, runner.py,
  final.py, tests/test_offline.py, plus AGENTS.md
- Section 13: the MESO agent on this branch: arena_kit/agents/llm.py, claims.py, writing.py, play.py,
  run logs in runs/meso*/
Read files from the other branch with `git show feature/team-agent:negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/<path>`.
Port the code you need into this branch. Do not merge `feature/team-agent`.

## What to build
- A new agent, `arena_kit/agents/spec.py` (class `SpecAgent`), registered wherever the CLI picks up
  agents (`arena run` / `arena play`), so it runs the same way as the existing agents. Put shared
  logic in modules (levers, sheets, closing, clock, analyst), not in one big file.
- Code decides every number: anchors, steps, term sheets, accept and walk-away. The model writes words
  only (R9.1, R13.14-R13.15), and code-written fallbacks cover every model call (R10.1-R10.2,
  R12.17).
- Section 0.7 runs at case open: check the case file, compute C for every opening quote with
  standard terms filled in and C_alt for the alternative, check coverage, build the lever table,
  pick the playbook row, set anchor and floor, apply the must-have filter, start the clock. Never
  crash on a field outside the ranges in section 0. Log it and use the defaults.
- Merge R4.1 and R13.10 into one anchor table, as R13.10 asks. Write down the choice in a comment.
- Where two requirements conflict, the more specific one wins, and section 5's concession rules stay
  in charge (see the "Not taken from" notes). List every judgement call you make in DESIGN_NOTES.md.

## Tests
- Write every unit test listed under "Acceptance" in the requirements file, under tests/, using
  TeamAgent's offline tests as the template. Add one test that loads all 19 cases in
  data/practice_cases.json and runs the section 0.7 preparation without errors.
- Run the whole test suite. It must pass before you play anything.
- Then play the sandbox (D01, D02) and the local sim. Only after that play the 10 hosted practice
  cases (P01-P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18). The key is in starter-kit/.env, and the quota is 200
  sessions per 24 h, so don't loop on the hosted cases. Compare each score with the targets under
  "Acceptance" (mean 71.6, all 10 cases ending in a deal, each case closed within 420 s).

## Working rules
- Commit in small steps with clear messages, and push to `feature/spec-agent`. Don't touch main or
  the other feature branches.
- When a practice case scores below its target, read its replay and the run log, fix the cause,
  and record the cause and the fix in DESIGN_NOTES.md.
- At the end, report a per-case score table (new agent vs target), the requirements you did not
  implement or changed and why, and which tests pass.
</pasted_content id="72da">

     730 negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md

1	# New buyer agent - requirements
2	
3	What the next agent must do, taken from the three agents on `feature/team-agent` that hold the best
4	practice scores: `BuyerAgent` (`arena_kit/agents/buyer.py`, `arena_kit/strategy.py`,
5	`arena_kit/dossier.py`) for sections 1-10, `DualAgent` (`arena_kit/agents/dual.py`,
6	`arena_kit/intel.py`, `arena_kit/tactics.py`) for section 11, and `TeamAgent` (`team/agent.py`,
7	`team/levers.py`, `team/briefing.py`, `team/runner.py`, `team/final.py`; findings in `AGENTS.md`) for
8	section 12. Section 13 takes the MESO agent on this branch (`feature/meso-agent`:
9	`arena_kit/agents/llm.py`, `arena_kit/claims.py`, `arena_kit/writing.py`, `arena_kit/play.py`; run
10	logs in `runs/meso*/`). Each requirement is something that held up in the practice arena. Source
11	files in sections 1-12 refer to `feature/team-agent`.
12	
13	## 0. What the agent is given: the case JSON
14	
15	Everything the agent decides is computed from the case file (`POST /v1/sessions` → `case`, or
16	`GET /v1/cases?set=…`; the 19 practice files are in `data/practice_cases.json`) plus the suppliers'
17	opening quotes. Read every value from the file - never hard-code one - but expect the shapes and
18	ranges below: they hold in all 19 practice cases, and anything outside them is a signal to log and
19	fall back to defaults, not to crash. Source: `brief/api.md` (Case file, Terms, Cost and score).
20	
21	### 0.1 A real case file (`case:P01`)
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "case_id": "case:P01", "set": "practice", "type": "price_increase", "hosted": true,
26	  "title": "Brandlhuber announces +9.5 % on HN volute casings",
27	  "briefing": "You negotiate for Hollerau Pumpenwerke with Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG. ... Need: 8150 pc a year. Category goal: stabilise a strategic supply ... Fallback if you walk away: the second-source quote quote:7200001. Must-haves: none. Prepare from the data package.",
28	  "trigger_doc": "doc:20260911-70110-P01",
29	  "parts": ["part:310010"],
30	  "suppliers": ["sup:70110"],
31	  "negotiable": ["unit_price", "effective_date", "payment_days"],
32	  "fixed_terms": {"lead_time_days": 42, "volume_per_year": 8150, "contract_months": 12,
33	                  "index_clause": null, "incoterm": "FCA", "tooling_eur": 0},
34	  "term_options": {"effective_date": ["2026-11-01", "2027-01-01", "2027-04-01"],
35	                   "payment_days": [14, 30, 45, 60, 90]},
36	  "buyer": {
37	    "need_per_year": 8150, "horizon_years": 1.0,
38	    "current_unit_price": 126.53, "fallback_unit_price": 136.65,
39	    "interest_rate": 0.08, "reference_payment_days": 60,
40	    "need_lead_time_days": 45, "late_cost_per_day": 420, "cost_per_defect": 216,
41	    "category_goal": "stabilise",
42	    "fallback_risk_pct": 10, "index_risk_pct": 4,
43	    "sustainable_margin_pct": 3, "relationship_eur_per_point": 15470,
44	    "freight_eur_per_unit": {"EXW": 2.19, "FCA": 1.9, "DAP": 0.0},
45	    "index_paths": {},
46	    "must_haves": [],
47	    "alternative": {"kind": "quote", "ref": "quote:7200001",
48	                    "terms": {"unit_price": 143.22, "payment_days": 60, "lead_time_days": 70,
49	                              "volume_per_year": 8150, "contract_months": 12,
50	                              "effective_date": "2027-01-01", "index_clause": null,
51	                              "incoterm": "FCA", "tooling_eur": 1500, "ppm_commitment": 2376}}
52	  },
53	  "round_limit": 10,
54	  "refs": ["doc:20260911-70110-P01", "ctr:4600070110", "sc:70110@2026Q3", "quote:7200001"]
55	}
56	```
57	
58	### 0.2 Top-level fields: what to expect, what uses it
59	
60	| Field | Expect | Used by |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| `case_id`, `set` | `case:P01`…`P19` (practice), `case:D01`/`D02` (sandbox), hidden IDs in `final` | cache keys (R13.17), logs |
63	| `hosted` | practice only; `true` on the 10 playable cases (P01-P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18) | - |
64	| `type` | `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` | `TYPE_LEVERS` (R1.5), case questions (R9.4), anchor (R4.1, R13.12) |
65	| `title`, `briefing` | prose; repeats need, goal, need lead time, fallback and must-haves in words. The structured `buyer` block is the source of truth - never parse numbers from the briefing | profile prompt (R1.3), writer context (R9.2) |
66	| `trigger_doc` | a `doc:` ID (the supplier's letter / RFQ document) | data arguments - notice vs contract (R13.9) |
67	| `parts` | 1 part, except bundling (P07: 4, P15: 3) - still **one** `unit_price` per sheet | dossier (R1.1), should-cost (R2.1) |
68	| `suppliers` | 1 supplier; 2-3 = an RFQ (P05: 3, P06: 2; sandbox D02: 2) | RFQ handling (sections 8, 12.6) |
69	| `negotiable` | always contains `unit_price`, plus 2-3 of the fields below. A term sheet must carry **exactly** these fields or it is a `422` | sheets (R6, R11.11), lever table (R12.3) |
70	| `fixed_terms` | the case's other fields with their values (fields named in neither list - e.g. `ppm_commitment` outside quality cases - take the supplier's standard terms) | C computation, `describe` (R13.14) |
71	| `term_options` | allowed values per negotiable field except `unit_price` - send nothing else | lever table (R12.3), steps (R13.1), repair (R11.9) |
72	| `round_limit` | 10 in every case so far - read it, do not assume it | horizon H (R5.1), close rules (R7.5-R7.6) |
73	| `refs` | 3-5 starting IDs (`doc`, `ctr`, `sc`, `quote`); "a start, not the whole story" | dossier (R1.1), arguments (R9.5) |
74	| `facts` | **hidden cases only**: case-specific facts in `facts.json` format, citable in that case | merge into the claim data before computing arguments (R13.9) |
75	| `wave`, `theme`, `open`, `seconds_left` | **final only**; `seconds_left` until the 8-minute wave cap | case clock (R11.14-R11.16) - read `seconds_left`, don't assume 480 |
76	
77	### 0.3 Negotiable fields and their options (all practice cases)
78	
79	| Field | Options seen | Notes |
80	|---|---|---|
81	| `unit_price` | free, EUR with 2 decimals | the only free field |
82	| `payment_days` | always `[14, 30, 45, 60, 90]` | reference is 60; fixed at 30-60 where not negotiable |
83	| `contract_months` | always `[12, 24, 36]` | with `horizon_years` = 2, 12 months leaves half the need uncovered (R12.2) |
84	| `volume_per_year` | three steps around the need, e.g. `[16379, 19890, 23400]` (≈ 70 / 85 / 100 % or 80 / 100 / 120 %) | where fixed it equals `need_per_year` |
85	| `effective_date` | `["2026-11-01", "2027-01-01", "2027-04-01"]` (price_increase) | the horizon starts at the earliest option; later = more units at `current_unit_price` |
86	| `lead_time_days` | 3-5 values, e.g. `[28, 35, 42, 56]` | compare with `need_lead_time_days`; often a must-have |
87	| `index_clause` | `null` + one series at deadband 0 / 3 / 5 %, fixed `material_share` (0.2-0.8) and `base_month` `"2026-08"` | the clause object must match an option exactly |
88	| `ppm_commitment` | `[300, 800, 1500, 2500]` (quality) | priced with `cost_per_defect` and the chargeback |
89	| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | `[0, 150, 300, 500]` (quality) | capped at `cost_per_defect` in C |
90	| `tooling_eur` | `[0, 7500, 15000]` (P06) | one-off, added to C |
91	| `incoterm` | `EXW` / `FCA` / `DAP`; fixed in every practice case | freight from `freight_eur_per_unit`; DAP is always 0.0 |
92	
93	### 0.4 The `buyer` block: what to expect
94	
95	| Field | Range seen | Pattern to rely on |
96	|---|---|---|
97	| `need_per_year` | 3,420 - 94,800 | units; with `horizon_years` the total need = N × H |
98	| `horizon_years` | `1` / `1.0` or `2` / `2.0` (API allows ≤ 3) | int **or** float - normalise; 1-year cases have `contract_months` fixed at 12 |
99	| `current_unit_price` | 4.20 - 412.74 | equals the fallback price in an RFQ (new part) |
100	| `fallback_unit_price` | 1.00 - 1.25 × current | 1.25 × in the capacity cases: walking is expensive |
101	| `interest_rate` | always 0.08 | our cost of money (R2.2) |
102	| `reference_payment_days` | always 60 | paying earlier than 60 days costs us interest |
103	| `need_lead_time_days`, `late_cost_per_day` | 5-59 days; EUR 40-2,400/day | capacity cases carry the high late cost |
104	| `cost_per_defect` | 0 - 780 | 0 in raw_material cases: ppm is worthless there |
105	| `category_goal` | `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage`, `routine` | selects the playbook row (R13.10) and the anchor cut (R4.1) |
106	| `fallback_risk_pct` | follows the goal: leverage 3, routine 5, quality_first 8, stabilise 10, secure_supply 25 | uncovered need is the costliest mistake in secure_supply |
107	| `index_risk_pct` | follows the goal: leverage 1, routine / quality_first 2, secure_supply 3, stabilise 4 | a clause costs us this share of indexed spend on top of the path |
108	| `sustainable_margin_pct`, `relationship_eur_per_point` | 0.5-10 %; EUR 5,000-31,920 per point-year - **only** for stabilise and secure_supply, `null` otherwise | the margin charge (R2.3, R13.8); treat `null` as "no charge" |
109	| `freight_eur_per_unit` | `{EXW, FCA, DAP}`, DAP always 0.0 | per committed unit |
110	| `index_paths` | `{}` or one series: `AS-14404` +0.06, `CU-NOTATION` +0.05, `PPI-C241` +0.03 | the expected move of the clause's series; a series missing here has path 0 |
111	| `must_haves` | `[]` or one rule: `lead_time_days <= 42` (P05, P09), `<= 84` (P06), `volume_per_year >= 22230` (P10), `ppm_commitment <= 1500` (P11) | a deal that breaks one scores **0** - check every sheet and every accept against them (R6.7, R11.9) |
112	| `alternative` | `kind` = `quote` (`ref` = `quote:72000NN`, full `terms`), `current_contract` (`ref` = a `ctr:` ID **or `null`**, full `terms`), or `none` (`ref` null, `terms` `{}`) | C_alt = C(alternative terms); with `none`, no deal = uncovered need at the fallback price, score 0 |
113	
114	### 0.5 Case types as they appear
115	
116	| Type | Goals seen | Negotiable besides price | Typical must-have / alternative |
117	|---|---|---|---|
118	| `price_increase` | stabilise, leverage | effective_date, payment_days, index_clause or volume | quote or none |
119	| `renewal` | stabilise, routine | payment_days, contract_months, volume, index_clause | quote or none; H = 2 |
120	| `rfq` | leverage, stabilise | payment_days, lead_time_days, tooling_eur | lead-time must-have; `alternative: none` |
121	| `bundling` | routine | payment_days, contract_months | `current_contract`; 3-4 parts, one price |
122	| `raw_material` | leverage | index_clause, payment_days, contract_months | quote; `index_paths` set; `cost_per_defect` 0 |
123	| `capacity` | secure_supply | volume_per_year, lead_time_days, contract_months / payment_days | volume or lead-time must-have; fallback 1.25 × |
124	| `quality` | quality_first | ppm_commitment, chargeback, (lead_time_days) | ppm must-have or `current_contract` |
125	
126	A hidden case may combine these differently or bring a new type: take the levers from `negotiable`
127	when `type` is unknown, and the `routine` playbook row when `category_goal` is unknown.
128	
129	### 0.6 The opening quotes and the replies
130	
131	`POST /v1/sessions` also returns `opening`, one entry per supplier:
132	
133	```json
134	"sup:70240": {"offer_id": "offer:70240-0", "round": 0, "status": "open",
135	              "terms": {"unit_price": 31.5, "lead_time_days": 52},
136	              "alternatives": [],
137	              "missing_fields": ["payment_days"],
138	              "claims": [], "claim_results": [],
139	              "signals": {"reply_delay_days": 4, "validity_days": 30},
140	              "text": "Hello, Thank you for your enquiry. ..."}
141	```
142	
143	- **`terms` can be partial.** Fields in `missing_fields` close on the supplier's **standard terms**
144	  (in the quote PDF) - fill them from the PDF before computing C; never assume our reference values.
145	- **An opening quote can break a must-have** (P05: 52 days against `<= 42`) - repair it (R11.9).
146	- `alternatives`: `[{offer_id, terms}]` - extra packages, acceptable like the main sheet (R12.11).
147	- Replies (`POST …/messages`) carry `status` (`open`, `final_offer`, `agreed`, `walked_away`,
148	  `no_bid`), `term_sheets` (its standing offer, `offer:` ID), `claim_results` per argument,
149	  `signals`, `missing_fields` and `attachments` (cost breakdown XLSX, 8D PDF, delivery schedule).
150	
151	### 0.7 What to compute from the case JSON before the first message
152	
153	1. Validate: every `negotiable` field except `unit_price` has `term_options`; no field is both
154	   fixed and negotiable; must-haves name real fields.
155	2. C(terms) with `arena_kit.total_cost`, the opening C of every supplier (standard terms filled),
156	   and C_alt from `buyer.alternative`.
157	3. Coverage: does `contract_months` × `volume_per_year` cover `need_per_year` × `horizon_years`?
158	   If an option closes the gap and lowers C, it goes into message 1 (R12.1-R12.2).
159	4. The lever table (R12.3) over `term_options`, the playbook row for `category_goal` (R13.10), the
160	   anchor (R4, R13.12) and the floor (R2.1, R6.5).
161	5. The must-have filter every sheet and every accept passes through.
162	6. The clock: `round_limit` and, in the final, `seconds_left`.
163	
164	## Evidence
165	
166	From `knowledge/sessions.jsonl` on `feature/team-agent` (practice sessions, 10 Oct 2026).
167	
168	### Where BuyerAgent was better
169	
170	| Case | Type / goal | BuyerAgent | DualAgent (best of its runs) | Why BuyerAgent did as well or better |
171	|---|---|---|---|---|
172	| P11 | quality / quality_first | **0.589** | 0.536 (3 runs) | Same price (EUR 46.00), quality cost EUR 5,724 vs 10,732; it kept going (7 e-mails) where DualAgent closed on "deadlock" after 5 |
173	| P18 | raw_material / leverage | **0.419** | 0.319 (3 runs) | Price EUR 260,700 vs 265,440; index clause EUR 1,173 vs 7,167; supplier conceded 9.8 % vs 8.2 % and answered "counter" in rounds 1-3 (DualAgent drew "hold" in rounds 2-3) |
174	| P01 | price_increase / stabilise | 0.931 | 0.941 | Within 0.01; no early-payment cost in its last two runs (DualAgent paid ~EUR 7.2k in 4 of 5 runs) |
175	| P04, P10 | - | 0.860, 0.655 | 0.860, 0.655 | Tie |
176	
177	### Where DualAgent was better
178	
179	| Case | Type / goal | DualAgent | BuyerAgent | Why DualAgent did better |
180	|---|---|---|---|---|
181	| P01 | price_increase / stabilise | **0.941** (best of all runs) | 0.931 | Data argument twice, rapport, an appreciative close; deal at 135.20 with the price from April 2027 |
182	| P02 | price_increase / stabilise | **0.385** | 0.211 | Kept the supplier healthy: relationship charge EUR 92 vs **124,110**, no index risk (BuyerAgent: EUR 17,158). BuyerAgent's lower price (351 vs 373) cost far more than it saved |
183	| P03 | renewal / stabilise | **0.919** (same in 3 runs) | 0.900 | Lower total spend (EUR 3,959,776 vs 3,967,013) in 4 e-mails instead of 6 |
184	| P05 | rfq / leverage | **0.444** | 0.372 | Talked to all three bidders (2-3 e-mails each), cited the cheaper rival, closed with the cheapest bidder (70240) - BuyerAgent wrote only once to it and closed with 70210 |
185	| P07 | bundling / routine | **0.721** | 0.702 | EUR 5.45 vs 5.48 after 5 e-mails, appreciative close |
186	| P08 | raw_material / leverage | **0.343** | 0.332 | EUR 5.61 vs 5.67 |
187	
188	The runs were hours apart (BuyerAgent 18:4x, DualAgent 21:xx) and the shared `strategy.py` changed
189	in between, so part of a gap can come from the code version, not the agent design. Section 11 takes
190	only what is DualAgent's own.
191	
192	### Where TeamAgent was better
193	
194	TeamAgent's runs are not in `sessions.jsonl` (it logs through `team.evaluate`). These best runs
195	(`runs/best_runs.json`, `runs/best_replays/`) are its own by their e-mails: the signature
196	"Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing" from its prompt, its code-written planned-move text word for word
197	(P10), and run times matching its commits (v4-v9, 10 Oct 18:00-01:30). P07 is the least certain.
198	
199	| Case | Type / goal | TeamAgent | DualAgent | BuyerAgent | What won it |
200	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
201	| P05 | rfq / leverage | **0.781** | 0.444 | 0.372 | All three bidders in message 1; each told the cheapest rival's offer ID and price ("we did not know that - a fair point"); lead time repaired to the must-have; payment probed with 90/60/30 sheets; two bidders `agreed` in round 2, it took the cheaper (EUR 28.42 vs 30.39) |
202	| P08 | raw_material / leverage | **0.549** | 0.343 | 0.332 | 24-month cover of the 2-year need from message 1 (the quote was 12 months); answered "we cannot fix the price for two years" with a 5 % deadband index clause instead of 0 %; accepted the final offer |
203	| P07 | bundling / routine | **0.773** | 0.721 | 0.702 | 24- and 36-month packages from message 1, payment 90 days from the contract (ctr:4600070610); a step every round; accepted the final offer at EUR 5.37 |
204	| P10 | capacity / secure_supply | **0.671** | 0.655 | 0.655 | Full need (23,400/year) for 24 months in message 1, with a lead-time trade; accepted the final offer |
205	| P04 | renewal / routine | 0.860 | 0.860 | 0.860 | Tie: full requirement, 24 months, 90 days in message 1 |
206	
207	The team's practice average (mean of 10 cases × 100, 8-minute cap): v2 13.3 (pushed past final
208	offers, walk-aways) → v4 56.3 (accept final offers) → **v9 56.9 with all 10 deals**.
209	
210	### Where the MESO agent was better
211	
212	From `runs/meso3/` (11 Oct 02:52) and `runs/meso4/` (11 Oct 03:25) on `feature/meso-agent`:
213	
214	| Case | Type / goal | MESO | Best before | What won it |
215	|---|---|---|---|---|
216	| P11 | quality / quality_first | **0.710** (meso3 and meso4) | 0.672 | Step 1 offered 300 / 800 / 1,500 ppm at equal cost; the supplier took **300 ppm** (the earlier best deal had 1,500 ppm). Step 2 settled the chargeback, then 3 price rounds. Same deal in both runs |
217	| P18 | raw_material / leverage | **0.453** (meso3) | 0.419 | Step 1: payment 90 / 30 / 45 days at equal cost → 90 locked; step 2: index clause options → locked; then one price round and the final offer at EUR 5.40 |
218	| P03 | renewal / stabilise | 0.919 (meso3) | 0.919 | Tie with DualAgent's best |
219	
220	### MESO failures not to repeat
221	
222	- **P10, 0.0 (meso4):** no coverage move in message 1; the final offer kept 19,890/year for 12
223	  months, nothing was acceptable, it walked. TeamAgent's 0.671 put the full need for 24 months into
224	  message 1 (R12.2).
225	- **P04, 0.056 (meso4):** accepted a 12-month final offer on a 2-year need - the same failure as
226	  DualAgent's P04 (R11.17, R12.2).
227	- **P05, 0.0 (meso3):** accepted the best final offer 4.5 minutes after its thread's last move,

235	### DualAgent failures not to repeat
236	
237	- **P04, 0.056:** accepted a final offer that covered only half the need (EUR 94,000 uncovered need +
238	  4,700 fallback risk). Its other two P04 runs scored 0.86.
239	- **P05, 0.0:** one e-mail to one bidder, then accepted 70210 at its opening EUR 36.00 ("their offer
240	  meets our target"); the two other bidders were never written to.
241	- **P11 and P18:** P11 closed itself on "deadlock" with terms still open; on P18 it held twice, the
242	  supplier held back, and the final offer came after 4 e-mails (see the BuyerAgent table above).
243	
244	## 1. Prepare before the clock
245	
246	- **R1.1 Supplier dossier.** Before the session's first move, gather for every supplier everything
247	  in the data package: call and meeting notes, letters, past negotiations (asked vs settled), its
248	  financials, our payment record, scorecards, should-cost, the part's cost drivers and contract
249	  clauses (`dossier.gather`, Sunday release included). Cache it per supplier and parts.
250	- **R1.2 Cash signals.** Scan the dossier for cash-pressure words (cash, liquidity, skonto, prepay,
251	  credit line, working capital, insolvency, short-time work, "within N days") and record the hits.
252	- **R1.3 One profile call per supplier, in parallel.** A model reads the dossier plus the computed
253	  data arguments and returns JSON only:
254	  `persona, tone, pressures[], wants[], levers[], avoid[], cash_short, claim_ranking[], questions[], angle`.
255	  Timeout 90 s for all profiles together.
256	- **R1.4 Validate the profile.** `levers` are mapped onto the case's negotiable field names and
257	  `claim_ranking` onto real argument keys; anything that does not match is dropped. `cash_short` is
258	  true if the model says so, or if the dossier has cash signals and payment_days is the top lever.
259	- **R1.5 Default profile.** If the call fails or times out, use a default profile: polite, factual,
260	  constructive tone; levers = payment_days first when cash signals exist, then the case type's levers
261	  (`TYPE_LEVERS` below). A missing profile never costs the case.
262	
263	`TYPE_LEVERS`: price_increase → effective_date, payment_days · raw_material → index_clause,
264	payment_days, contract_months · renewal → contract_months, volume_per_year, payment_days · bundling →
265	contract_months, payment_days · capacity → volume_per_year, lead_time_days, contract_months ·
266	quality → chargeback_eur_per_complaint, ppm_commitment · rfq → payment_days, lead_time_days, tooling_eur.
267	
268	## 2. Our estimate of the supplier
269	
270	- **R2.1 Full cost, calibrated.** In this order: the supplier's own cost-breakdown XLSX (sum of EUR
271	  elements, without margin and totals); else should-cost / 1.02 (fits the arena's relationship charge
272	  over 31 recorded deals - `FULL_COST_K` in `team/agent.py` and the current MESO agent); else opening
273	  price / 1.10. Not too high: a high floor made BuyerAgent stop pushing (P01, 10 Oct: accepted 136.30
274	  where 133.70 was reachable). Not too low either: with its "low end of the confidence band"
275	  estimate BuyerAgent saw no cost in squeezing P02's supplier to EUR 351 - the arena charged EUR
276	  124,110 for it (score 0.211; DualAgent 0.385 at EUR 373).
277	- **R2.2 Cost of money.** The buyer's interest rate, plus 6 points for a supplier short of cash.
278	  Once the supplier has priced payment days itself (two of its sheets differ only in payment), use
279	  that revealed rate instead (slope × 360, clamped to 3-40 %) - see R12.4.
280	- **R2.3 Margin charge only where the goal has one.** C includes the supplier's margin penalty only
281	  for stabilise and secure_supply.
282	
283	## 3. What we negotiate on
284	
285	- **R3.1 Best sheet on the table.** For each thread, take the supplier's cheapest offer for us among
286	  its standing sheet *and* its alternatives, preferring ones that keep the must-haves.
287	- **R3.2 Both-sides-gain structure (`mutual_combo`).** Move each of the supplier's non-price terms
288	  toward what the supplier prefers for as long as that also lowers our C (e.g. a longer contract that
289	  covers our whole need). The price is negotiated on this structure, not on the quote as sent.
290	- **R3.3 Asks are never free (`reference_combo`).** Terms the supplier pulled beyond our reference
291	  (payment days, volume, contract length, lead time, no index clause) are put back where that saves
292	  us money before pricing the target - what it asks for is paid for in price.
293	
294	## 4. The opening anchor
295	
296	- **R4.1 Anchor from the data.** The lowest of: the goal's cut off the best quote (leverage 12 %,
297	  routine 8 %, quality_first 6 %, stabilise 6 %, secure_supply 5 %); the current price (no increase
298	  at all) for price_increase and raw_material cases; the fair price = should-cost / (1 − margin)
299	  (leverage 5 %, routine 6 %, quality_first 8 %; the sustainable margin for relationship goals).
300	- **R4.2 Credibility limits.** Never more than 25 % under the supplier's price; never under its
301	  estimated full cost × 1.01; never under the price at which C stops falling.
302	- **R4.3 RFQ.** Every bidder is anchored to the best quote in the case, not its own (D02: anchored
303	  to its own 17.10, the dearer bidder agreed to 15.09 at once; about 13 was reachable).
304	- **R4.4 Fixed anchor.** The anchor is set once per thread.
305	
306	## 5. Concessions: reciprocal, never stuck
307	
308	- **R5.1 Curve.** Our k-th offer closes `1 − (1 − k/H)^1.6` of the gap from the anchor to the
309	  supplier's C; H = 6 (5 in an RFQ). Steps shrink over time.
310	- **R5.2 Reciprocity.** Track the supplier's C after every reply (one entry per reply, so a hold shows
311	  as a zero step). If it moved more than 0.1 % of C: our step = max(min(planned, 0.5 × its step),
312	  0.4 % of C). We move by less than it did, but always visibly.
313	- **R5.3 Deadlock breaker (the key difference from DualAgent).** If the supplier did not move, hold
314	  **once**; the next round make one real step to break the deadlock: at least 15 % of the C gap left
315	  (TeamAgent's measure, R12.5), and never less than 0.4 % of C. Never stall two rounds, never close
316	  just because both sides held. Never a token step (D01: "a nominal adjustment of one cent" was
317	  called out).
318	- **R5.4 Still moving means ask again.** If the supplier's offer meets our target but it is still
319	  conceding (> 0.4 % of C last round) and more than 3 rounds are left, set the target to
320	  `their C − 0.5 × their last step` and keep negotiating.
321	- **R5.5 Caps.** The target never exceeds 0.995 × the alternative's C. In an RFQ it is at most 0.99 ×
322	  the best rival's C, and never below the anchor.
323	
324	## 6. Term sheets
325	
326	- **R6.1 Up to three sheets, all at the target C** (`strategy.sheets`): our terms (every term at its
327	  best for us, at a higher price), their terms (the both-sides-gain structure), and a give (one lever
328	  from the profile moved toward the supplier, for a lower price). "Our terms" goes first.
329	- **R6.2 Shared surplus on a give.** When a term is worth more to the supplier than it costs us (e.g.
330	  faster payment to a cash-short supplier), price the give halfway between our equal-cost price and the
331	  supplier's indifference price (`give_price`, `SURPLUS_SHARE = 0.5`). Both sides are better off
332	  taking it.
333	- **R6.3 The supplier asked for something.** Send two sheets instead: exactly its ask at a lower
334	  price (shared surplus), and our reference terms at the target price. No third sheet that blurs the
335	  trade (`ask_sheets`).
336	- **R6.4 Decoy.** Arrange the sheets as lean / recommended / other. The lean one is the recommended
337	  sheet 2 % cheaper with the supplier's most-valued term moved our way, so the middle one looks
338	  sensible. It is safe: if the supplier takes the lean one, that is better for us (`with_decoy`).
339	- **R6.5 Sheet floor.** No sheet below max(estimated full cost × 0.97, 75 % of the supplier's price).
340	  P18, 10 Oct: a give at 28 % under was not credible and the supplier did not move.
341	- **R6.6 Out of reach.** If no sheet fits the target, send the supplier's own terms at
342	  max(floor, 99 % of its price), provided the must-haves hold.
343	- **R6.7 Every sheet keeps the must-haves** and is cheaper than what the supplier asks.
344	
345	## 7. When to close
346	
347	Accept the cheapest standing sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats the alternative when:
348	
349	- **R7.1** the supplier agreed to our terms;
350	- **R7.2** it made a final offer (single thread; in an RFQ only if every thread is final or this is
351	  the best offer on the table);
352	- **R7.3** its offer meets our next target - unless it is still moving with more than 3 rounds left
353	  (R5.4);
354	- **R7.4** its offer is as good as what we last offered;
355	- **R7.5** at most one round is left in the thread (or in every RFQ thread);
356	- **R7.6** the planned rounds are over (H + 2 offers in every thread).
357	
358	Walk away only when nothing on the table is acceptable and every thread is at a final offer or out of
359	rounds. **No** deadlock close and **no** walk-risk close: those ended DualAgent's P11 and P18 early.
360	
361	## 8. RFQ handling
362	
363	- **R8.1** Plan every live thread each round and write all their e-mails in parallel, so no thread
364	  idles into the 60-second rule.
365	- **R8.2** With more than two live threads, stop answering bidders more than 25 % dearer than the
366	  best once we have sent them two offers.
367	- **R8.3** Rival prices are cited as checkable arguments (`offer:` IDs), once per supplier.
368	
369	## 9. The e-mail
370	
371	- **R9.1 The model writes words only** (the kit's `writing.SYSTEM` JSON parts: salutation, opening,
372	  argument keys, bridge, question, closing). Code inserts the arguments word for word and the options
373	  paragraph from the term sheets, then lints (no leaks, no figures that are not in the material, no
374	  unknown IDs).
375	- **R9.2 What the writer sees:** the supplier's profile (persona, tone, pressures, wants, avoid,
376	  angle); its last e-mail with sender, status, subject and non-quote attachments; how our arguments
377	  have checked out so far; our last two e-mails; how far it moved toward us in % since our last
378	  e-mail; the options; up to 6 arguments ranked by the profile's `claim_ranking`; the questions.
379	- **R9.3 Plain stance per move** (`_stance`):
380	  - first e-mail: "We open: our options are ambitious; give the reasons, not apologies."
381	  - hold while they are still coming down: acknowledge the step briefly, say the price is still too
382	    high and why;
383	  - hold because they did not move: polite but firm, do not thank them for flexibility they did not
384	    show, give one concrete reason or ask what would let them move;
385	  - step: "a modest step - this costs us and we expect a step back."
386	- **R9.4 Questions.** One per e-mail at most, never repeated: a cost breakdown once (unless already
387	  asked or received - an open supplier sends one, and R2.1 uses it), then the case type's question
388	  (8D report, delivery schedule, shortest lead time, which cost elements rose, which volume or term
389	  would improve the price, bundle parts, fair base month and deadband), then the profile's questions.
390	- **R9.5 Arguments.** From `claims.candidates` (code-computed, checked IDs). Each ID once per case;
391	  an argument that came back `contradicted` is never used again; news the profile ranks as helpful
392	  counts as favourable. Even a fallback e-mail carries the two best arguments.
393	- **R9.6 Company name** from the data, else from the supplier's subject ("Quote from X:") or
394	  signature - never the bare supplier ID (D02: "Dear colleagues at sup:DEMO-J1").
395	- **R9.7 Allowed figures** come only from the supplier's e-mails, the trigger letter, the contract
396	  clauses, our arguments and the options paragraph.
397	
398	## 10. Robustness and timing
399	
400	- **R10.1** The writer has 35 s; a late or failed call is replaced by a code-written plain e-mail
401	  with the same sheets and arguments.
402	- **R10.2** A planning error falls back to the naive move; a hung model call never holds the case.
403	- **R10.3** Record every argument's `claim_results` and feed them into the next round.
404	- **R10.4** Log per move: target C, the supplier's C, the estimate, each sheet with its C, the prompt,
405	  the reply, dropped sentences and the close reason.

408	
409	### 11.1 A background analyst per supplier thread (`intel.Analyst`)
410	
411	- **R11.1 Two layers per supplier e-mail.** At once, by code: standing sheet and its move since the
412	  last round, status, signals (reply delay, quote validity), claim results, missing fields, who wrote
413	  (role), offers stated only in prose, cost drivers the supplier names ("LCI-C rose 2.7 % ... 30 % of
414	  our cost"), a rough tone. In the background, one model extraction call per e-mail (JSON): the same
415	  items read better, plus constraints, lever hints, relationship style, withdraw language.
416	- **R11.2 The model reads, it never sets a number.** Every figure the extraction returns must appear
417	  in the e-mail, or it is dropped.
418	- **R11.3 Short grace, never late.** The negotiator waits at most 12 s for the model layer, then
419	  uses whatever snapshot is ready.
420	- **R11.4 Turn the supplier's own drivers against its ask.** Weight each named driver by its cost
421	  share (Σ change × share) and compare with the increase asked for (`cost_gap_pct`). Every index the
422	  supplier names that the data covers becomes a checked argument (`new_claims`), favourable when it
423	  rose ≤ 1 % or less than half the increase asked for. P01's 0.941 opened this way: "the weighted
424	  effect is about +2.4 %, not the 9.5 % you ask for".
425	- **R11.5 Walk risk as a signal, not a close rule.** Score 0..1 from: final offer, price unchanged
426	  1-2 rounds, rising reply delay, shrinking quote validity, escalation to the boss, a drop in tone,
427	  withdraw language. Use it only to (a) switch to an appreciative close tone (≥ 0.4) and (b) put a
428	  better prose offer of the supplier's on the table (R11.8, ≥ 0.5). It does **not** close the case
429	  (R7 still decides).
430	- **R11.6 New parts.** Parts named in the supplier's e-mails beyond the case file get a dossier too.

432	### 11.2 More from the supplier's own words
433	
434	- **R11.7 Asks from the e-mail, not only the sheet.** `supplier_asks` also takes the analyst's lever
435	  hints ("we need payment within 15 days"), snaps the number to the case's options and treats it as an
436	  ask (R6.3) when it costs us something. A supplier asking for faster payment is marked cash-short and
437	  the estimate is redone with the higher cost of money (R2.2).
438	- **R11.8 Lock in prose offers.** When the supplier states a better offer only in its text (not in a
439	  term sheet) and it keeps the must-haves and beats the alternative, send it back as our first term
440	  sheet - at once if it meets our target, or under pressure (≤ 2 rounds left, walk risk ≥ 0.5, or the
441	  case clock near its end). The arena accepts only standing sheets, so this turns words into a deal.
442	
443	### 11.3 Sheets
444	
445	- **R11.9 Repair broken must-haves before building sheets.** Move each must-have field in the
446	  supplier's terms to the nearest allowed value that keeps it (P05: a 52-day lead time against
447	  "≤ 42" left no sheet to send).
448	- **R11.10 Hold the cost, not the sheets.** When we hold (R5.3), rebuild the sheets on the supplier's
449	  new terms at the same target C. Sending the same three sheets again read as "no adjustments" and drew
450	  a final offer (P04, 10 Oct).
451	- **R11.11 Code's last word on every sheet** (`_guard_sheets`): costs us at most the target, is
452	  cheaper for us than the supplier's standing offer, is not one of the supplier's own sheets, keeps
453	  the must-haves. If nothing survives, send our last sheets rather than nothing.
454	
455	### 11.4 Wording tactics (words only)
456	
457	- **R11.12 One tactic per e-mail, picked by code** from the analyst's snapshot (`tactics.pick`). It
458	  changes the words, never the sheets, and every tactic has code-written lines so it still shows when
459	  the model is slow. Keep the rules that won:
460	  - `competitive_pressure` only in an RFQ or with a real cheaper rival offer, never an invented rival
461	    (P05 0.444);
462	  - `data_argument` when the supplier's own drivers explain over 1 point less than it asks, or unused
463	    checked arguments remain (P01 0.941);
464	  - `lever_trade` for a cash-short supplier or one that named a term it cares about;
465	  - `appreciation_close` when the gap is under 1.5 % or walk risk ≥ 0.4 (P07 0.721, P01);
466	  - `humor_rapport` only with a relationship-driven supplier in a friendly tone, never with an
467	    annoyed one.
468	- **R11.13 Tactic and stance must agree.** `firm_disappointment` only after a real hold by the
469	  supplier (R9.3), and never at walk risk ≥ 0.4. `measured_lowball` / `firm_disappointment` were in
470	  the P18 run that drew "hold" twice: the deadlock breaker (R5.3) has priority over the tone.
471	
472	### 11.5 Case clock (Live Final)
473	
474	- **R11.14 Clock from case open.** No new counter-offer after 360 s, closed by 420 s, so every case
475	  ends inside the 8-minute wave cap.
476	- **R11.15 Measure the round time** (our send to the supplier's reply, last three rounds, each capped
477	  at 90 s; 45 s before any is measured) plus 10 s margin, and do not start a round that cannot finish
478	  before 420 s.
479	- **R11.16 After 360 s:** lock in a better prose offer if a round still fits (R11.8); repeat our last
480	  offer only when nothing on the table is acceptable yet; otherwise close by R7.

491	## 12. From TeamAgent
492	
493	### 12.1 Message 1 carries the deal
494	
495	- **R12.1 Put the whole structure into the first message.** Mined from ~80 recorded practice
496	  negotiations (`AGENTS.md`): the supplier's reply to our first message gained +0.46 score on
497	  average, replies 2-4 together +0.08. The first message already carries full coverage (R12.2), the
498	  payment variants, the rival's offer (RFQ) and the strongest arguments. Every best TeamAgent run
499	  (P04, P05, P07, P08, P10) did this.
500	- **R12.2 Coverage lock.** Commit the full need for the full horizon from message 1 whenever the
501	  lever table says covering it lowers C (P08: 24 months on a 2-year need; 12-month packages scored
502	  0.08 vs 0.44 there; P10: the volume was cut below the must-have in 4/4 runs without it). Once our
503	  sheet A covers the need, no sheet we send covers less - not even one the model writes. Trust the
504	  table when coverage does **not** pay: P08's fallback EUR 5.72 was below the offer's 5.98.
505	
506	### 12.2 Levers priced in euros
507	
508	- **R12.3 Lever table** (`team/levers.py`). For the supplier's standing sheet, move every negotiable
509	  field to each allowed option, and the price by 1 %; the change in C is the lever's value in EUR and
510	  in EUR per unit (`price_equiv`). Ask only for levers worth at least 0.3 % of C (coverage always
511	  counts): suppliers price every demand in, at 3-7× its value for faster lead time or chargebacks -
512	  ask only what the need requires.
513	- **R12.4 Revealed lever prices.** When two of the supplier's sheets (main and alternative) differ in
514	  one term, that pair is its own price for the term (`revealed_slopes`). With it, a lever counts only
515	  if it saves us more than the supplier charges for it; on a tie (within EUR 1) take the option closest
516	  to the supplier's own value - no stricter ask than needed. Its payment slope is its cost of money
517	  (R2.2).
518	
519	### 12.3 Anchor and steps
520	
521	- **R12.5 Steps in C, at least 15 % of the gap.** Mined: messages without a step drew a final offer
522	  37 % of the time, steps of at least 15 % of the gap 17 %. TeamAgent's path gives 0 / 15 / 30 / 45 /
523	  60 % of the gap from anchor to the supplier's C by our 1st ... 5th message, never less than 15 % of
524	  what was left after our last message, and never above 0.997 × the supplier's C. In this agent the
525	  15 % is the size of the deadlock-breaking step (R5.3) and the floor of a step we choose to make;
526	  the reciprocity cap (R5.2) still limits our step when the supplier moved less.
527	- **R12.6 RFQ anchor only falls.** The anchor is the lowest price anyone has put on the table in the
528	  case, cut by the goal's share plus 4 points for competition; in an RFQ it may move down when a
529	  rival goes lower, never up (R4.4 otherwise).
530	
531	### 12.4 Sheets
532	
533	- **R12.7 Payment probe.** One sheet of the first menu varies payment days (to the supplier's own
534	  value, or to 30 days) at equal C: its pick reveals its cost of money (P05: 90/60/30 sheets; the
535	  bidder came back at 30 days and EUR 28.42).
536	- **R12.8 Index clause on the supplier's terms.** When the supplier insists on an index clause, offer
537	  its own series with the deadband that costs us least, never a 0 % deadband we can avoid (P08: its
538	  0 % became 5 % in the final offer).
539	- **R12.9 A floor per structure.** Each variant has its own price floor - faster payment is worth
540	  more to the supplier, so that sheet may go lower. A give worth more than the price room (e.g. half
541	  the need uncovered) is no offer.
542	- **R12.10 Never regress.** Never send a sheet that costs us as much as one the supplier has already
543	  offered (within 0.1 %). If nothing cheaper is left: offer back its earlier, cheaper sheet once, else
544	  accept.
545	
546	### 12.5 Closing
547	
548	- **R12.11 Accept ladder.** Accept from every sheet the supplier ever offered in every live thread -
549	  main sheets and alternatives - cheapest valid first; up to three earlier IDs (cheaper by 0.1 %+)
550	  before the latest ones; a refused accept changes nothing, try the next. Mined: the cheapest sheet
551	  ever offered was often not the one taken (P01 7/7 runs: 0.586 vs 0.550); 30 % of replies carry an
552	  alternative, 38 % of those are cheaper for us than the main sheet.
553	- **R12.12 A final offer is accepted at once.** Any message after a `final_offer` → walked away 8/8;
554	  accepting it → deal 38/38. Only when nothing on the table is acceptable (it breaks a must-have or
555	  loses to our alternative) send **one** repair message: its price, accepted, with the nearest
556	  must-have-keeping option and full coverage (`confirm_final`).
557	- **R12.13 `agreed` or stalled → its earlier cheaper sheet, once.** `agreed` only echoes our last
558	  sheet: if one of its earlier sheets costs us 0.3 % less, offer exactly those terms back first.
559	  Stalled = no cheaper offer over its last three replies after 3+ of our messages.
560	
561	### 12.6 RFQ
562	
563	- **R12.14 First message by code, with the rival.** In an RFQ the first message to each bidder goes
564	  out without waiting for the model (three model calls at once would miss the clock) and carries the
565	  cheapest valid rival offer: "A competing supplier has offered EUR X per unit (offer:...)" (P05).
566	- **R12.15 Idle hopeless threads.** With 3+ live bidders, stop writing to one whose best valid sheet
567	  is more than 8 % dearer than the best anywhere and that moved less than 1 % in its last reply.
568	- **R12.16 Wait before an accept.** Before accepting in an RFQ, wait for replies still in flight from
569	  other bidders - one of them may be cheaper.
570	
571	### 12.7 Time and robustness
572	
573	- **R12.17 Model time budget.** The model gets 50 s minus the time since the supplier's reply minus
574	  15 s for every other thread with a call in flight; under 10 s left, the planned move goes out
575	  without it.
576	- **R12.18 Runner** (`team/runner.py`, `team/final.py`): one worker per supplier thread; calls retried,
577	  and a send that may have landed is checked against the arena before it is repeated; a worker never
578	  dies on an error; a case is done only when the arena ended the session; before a wave cap, close on
579	  the accept ladder; a crashed runner resumes its open sessions; `--check` pre-flight and `--rehearse`
580	  on the sandbox.

582	### 12.8 Data hygiene
583	
584	- **R12.19 Cash-short only from the supplier's own words**, never from our briefing labels or from
585	  its echo of our e-mail.
586	- **R12.20 Claims, sentence by sentence.** Drop a sentence whose IDs were all cited before (a repeat
587	  comes back `duplicate`: 18 % of TeamAgent's claims did before this rule); drop IDs the data does not have.
588	  Price-history claims (our past order prices) are context, not arguments: they "hold, but do not
589	  change our calculation" in 41 of 46 replies.
590	- **R12.21 Data attachment on request.** When the supplier asks for our figures ("which figures?",
591	  "send us the data", "verify this"), attach `our-figures.md`: every ID we cited with its values from
592	  the data package.
593	
594	### Not taken from TeamAgent
595	
596	- **The model proposing term sheets and accept/walk.** TeamAgent let the model re-mix the sheets and
597	  then clamped them back to the plan; here code decides every number (sections 5-7, R9.1). Its
598	  close rules (R12.11-R12.13) are code, and are taken.
599	- **The fixed 0/15/30/45/60 % schedule as the only concession rule**: the curve and reciprocity of
600	  section 5 stay; R12.5 sets the step size.
601	
602	## 13. From the MESO agent
603	
604	### 13.1 Settling terms one at a time
605	
606	- **R13.1 Sequential equal-cost steps for the heavy terms.** After coverage is set (R12.2), rank the
607	  remaining non-price terms by how many EUR they move C (the playbook's terms first, R13.10), skip any
608	  under 0.2 % of C, keep at most 3. Each message varies **one** term across up to three packages that
609	  all cost us the same C; the value the supplier answers with is locked, and the next message varies
610	  the next term; when every term is locked, only price is left. This is how the R6 sheets are built in
611	  the first rounds; R6's give / ask / decoy sheets apply in the price rounds and to asked-for terms.
612	  P11: 300 ppm locked from a 300 / 800 / 1,500 menu → 0.710 twice.
613	- **R13.2 Option order in a step:** the best option for us first, then the one the supplier asked for
614	  (if any), its current value, the middle option, the rest - three at most, each a different package.
615	- **R13.3 Reopen a costly lock.** A term stepped only once whose locked value costs us more than 1 %
616	  of C against its best option gets one more step (P01: the earliest effective date was worth 3.5 %
617	  of C).
618	- **R13.4 A step needs a choice.** A step with fewer than two credible packages (the rest under the
619	  floor or not cheaper than the supplier's sheet) is not a step: keep the term open, move it to the
620	  price round with our best value, or skip it - never "lock" a heavy term by sending it alone (P01,
621	  0.159).
622	- **R13.5 A term the supplier prices itself is locked without a step** (`revealed`): when its
623	  e-mail offers two packages that differ in one term only - its sheet and an "Alternatively, with
624	  30 days: EUR ..." line - lock that term at the value that costs us less at the supplier's own
625	  prices.
626	- **R13.6 Read the supplier's prose alternatives** (`prose_alternatives`): "Alternatively, with
627	  <terms>: EUR <price> per unit" in English and German (Zahlungsziel, Lieferzeit,
628	  Preisgleitklausel), for payment days, effective date, lead time, volume, contract months, ppm,
629	  chargeback and Incoterm; a line whose index clause cannot be pinned to an option is skipped. These
630	  packages feed R12.11 (accept ladder) and R13.5.
631	- **R13.7 No identical resend.** If the next message would only repeat our last sheets, the thread
632	  is done (a repeat draws a final offer) - close by R7 or offer back an earlier, cheaper sheet once.
633	
634	### 13.2 Correct numbers
635	
636	- **R13.8 Solve the price exactly.** Every package is priced so its C equals the target, not by a
637	  rule of thumb:
638	  - without the supplier's margin charge C is linear in the price: `p = (target − C(0)) / (C(1) − C(0))`;
639	  - with it, C is convex in the price: find the cheapest price by golden-section search between 0.5×
640	    and 1.5× the supplier's price, and solve for the target by bisection on the side **above** it
641	    (a price below the cheapest one costs more and leaves the supplier weaker).
642	  Tests: each sheet of a step has the same C within EUR 1.
643	- **R13.9 Data arguments computed the way the arena checks them** (`claims.py`): an index change uses
644	  two months of one series at most 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data
645	  (frozen at 2026-09); figures rounded as the sentence states them, next to their IDs. Only arguments
646	  that argue our side are offered: an index that **rose** confirms the supplier's case and is kept out
647	  unless it rose less than half the increase asked for (P02, P04). Kinds: index changes, the weighted
648	  summary of the part's own cost drivers ("explain about +x %, not y %", no ID), a letter giving less
649	  notice than the contract requires, scorecard quality and delivery, rival quotes and offers,
650	  should-cost, forecast volume. Each ID once per case; a rival's offer once per supplier.
651	
652	### 13.3 Playbook per category goal
653	
654	- **R13.10 One engine, settings per goal** (`PLAYBOOK`):
655	
656	  | Goal | Anchor (× opening) | Concede | Terms first | Index clause | Margin charge | Walk | Close gap |
657	  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
658	  | leverage | 0.85 | 0.85 | payment, index | any | no | yes | 0.5 % |
659	  | routine | 0.90 | 0.80 | contract months, payment | avoid | no | yes | 1.0 % |
660	  | stabilise | margin-optimal price | 0.80 | volume, contract months, payment | deadband ≥ 3 % | yes | no | 0.5 % |
661	  | secure_supply | 0.95 | 0.70 | volume, lead time, contract months | avoid | yes | no | 1.5 % |
662	  | quality_first | 0.92 | 0.80 | ppm, chargeback | avoid | no | yes | 0.5 % |
663	
664	  The anchors here and in R4.1 must be reconciled into one table before implementation (R4.1's cuts
665	  come from BuyerAgent and are data-driven; these are MESO's fixed shares). "Walk: no" means:
666	  stabilise and secure_supply take the best sheet that beats the alternative rather than walk.
667	- **R13.11 No index clause on a volatile series.** Never offer an index clause on a series that moved
668	  more than 15 % in its last 12 months - a clause on it is a bet.
669	- **R13.12 Price-increase anchor:** in a price_increase case the anchor is the current price - no
670	  increase at all - when it is below the quote.
671	- **R13.13 Accept on a small gap:** once only price is left, accept when the supplier's C is within
672	  the playbook's close gap of our target.
673	
674	### 13.4 The e-mail
675	
676	- **R13.14 Code writes what must match the sheets** (`writing.py`): the options paragraph is built
677	  from the term sheets themselves (`describe`: price, payment, effective date, months, volume, lead
678	  time, index clause with series, share, deadband and base month, ppm, chargeback, Incoterm, tooling),
679	  so prose and sheets never disagree; code adds its own sentences (a volume commitment, an earlier
680	  offer taken up) and the signature.
681	- **R13.15 Lint before sending.** Drop any sentence of the model's that leaks urgency, a deadline, a
682	  budget, a missing alternative ("no other supplier", "single source", "line stop", "fallback"), our
683	  limit ("walk-away price", "maximum we", "best we can pay"), "total cost", "category goal" or
684	  "score"; that carries a data ID; or that states a figure found nowhere in the material. Salutation by
685	  name only if that name appears in the supplier's e-mails, else "Dear colleagues at <company>". A
686	  volume question ("which volume can you commit?") is answered by code with the number from our sheet.
687	
688	### 13.5 Never lose a reply or an accept
689	
690	- **R13.16 Reply and accept inside 60 s.** A slow POST reads the supplier's reply from the thread
691	  instead of waiting on the call, so the 60-second rule is not missed (P05 once lost two agreed deals
692	  to replies held back this way). In an RFQ a final offer that is the best on the table is accepted
693	  within 60 s of its reply, even while other threads are still talking - waiting for in-flight
694	  replies (R12.16) never runs past that clock (P05, meso3: accepted after 4.5 minutes → `409`, no deal).
695	  On a `422` for an accept (the offer moved on) reload the thread and decide again.
696	- **R13.17 Cached data layer.** Build the master data file once (`arena-build-master-data`) and cache
697	  each case's negotiation dossier per data revision, so preparation for a case is a cache hit
698	  (milliseconds) and the Sunday release is picked up automatically.
699	
700	### Not taken from the MESO agent
701	
702	- **Locking whatever the supplier picks on a heavy term**, without R13.3/R13.4 (P01, 0.159).
703	- **The fixed `(1 − concede^k)` curve as the only concession rule** - section 5 (curve, reciprocity,
704	  deadlock breaker) stays. R13.10's `concede` column is MESO's pace per goal, a reference for tuning
705	  section 5's horizon per goal.
706	
707	## Acceptance
708	
709	- Unit tests for R5.2-R5.4 (reciprocity, deadlock breaker, still-moving), R6.2-R6.5 (surplus,
710	  ask sheets, decoy, floor) and R7 (close rules, including "no close on a two-round hold").
711	- Unit tests for R11.2 (figures not in the e-mail dropped), R11.8 (prose offer locked in), R11.9-R11.11
712	  (repair, rebuild on hold, sheet guard), R11.12 (no competitive pressure without a rival), R11.14-R11.15
713	  (clock) and R11.17-R11.18 (coverage, every RFQ bidder answered).
714	- Unit tests for R12.2 (coverage lock), R12.4 (revealed slopes), R12.10 (never regress), R12.11 (accept
715	  ladder order), R12.12 (final offer accepted, one repair only), R12.14 (RFQ message 1 cites the
716	  rival) and R12.17 (model budget). TeamAgent's offline tests on recorded negotiations
717	  (`team/tests/test_offline.py`) are the template.
718	- Unit tests for R13.1-R13.5 (one term per step, option order, reopen, a step needs two packages,
719	  revealed terms), R13.6 (prose alternatives in English and German), R13.7 (no identical resend),
720	  R13.8 (equal C within EUR 1, price above the C-minimum with the margin charge), R13.9 (index window,
721	  a rising index kept out), R13.11 (volatile series), R13.15 (lint) and R13.16 (an RFQ final offer
722	  accepted inside 60 s).
723	- Practice runs, the best recorded run per case (`runs/best_runs.json`, `runs/meso3`, `runs/meso4`):
724	  P01 ≥ 0.941, P02 ≥ 0.507, P03 ≥ 0.919, P04 ≥ 0.86, P05 ≥ 0.781, P07 ≥ 0.773, P08 ≥ 0.549,
725	  P10 ≥ 0.671, P11 ≥ 0.710, P18 ≥ 0.453 (mean 71.6). The P02 best run (0.507) is in no agent's
726	  session log and is not TeamAgent's; its e-mails use the shared writer, so it is probably a BuyerAgent
727	  or DualAgent run with logging off. Treat that target as a stretch goal.
728	- All 10 practice cases end in a deal (TeamAgent v9 did).
729	- Every message goes out within 60 s; no `contradicted` claims; no e-mail without a company name;
730	  every case closed by 420 s after it opens.

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - starter kit

A Python client for the arena API, two example buyer agents that negotiate by e-mail, helpers that
read the suppliers' documents and price a term sheet, a runner that plays many cases in parallel,
`arena-sim` - a local simulator of the arena's API - and a read-only MCP server over the data
package. Read the brief first
(`../brief/brief.md`); the full API is in `../brief/api.md`. Code: MIT.

## Quickstart - first agent on the board in 15 minutes

You need Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

**1. Get your team's key** (one per team): open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a
contact e-mail, and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once an organiser approves,
the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page (or its
link) shows it; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it. Keep it out of git.

```bash
cd starter-kit
uv sync --all-extras            # 2. install
cp .env.example .env            # 3. put ARENA_URL and your key (ARENA_API_KEY) into .env
uv run arena me                 # 4. your team and its practice quota
uv run arena cases              # 5. the practice cases (the 10 hosted ones are playable)
uv run arena play case:P01 -v   # 6. the naive agent negotiates one case
uv run arena board              # 7. you are on the practice leaderboard
```

Is the arena up? `curl $ARENA_URL/health`.

Step 6 prints the deal, your total cost `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the case score,
and a **replay link**: every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move, in words. That is
the learning loop - play a practice case, read the replay, improve your agent, play
again. In practice your best score per case counts, so play a case again whenever your agent improves.
**Quota:** 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours. `arena play` and `arena run` print
how many are left; `arena run` plays only the hosted practice cases and stops starting new ones
once the quota is used up (a `429` there does not go away by retrying). Plan your runs.

**Now the LLM agent.** Download the data (`ARENA_DATA=data/package` in `.env`), choose a model in
`.env` (your own key), then:

```bash
uv run arena data                                          # unpacks data/package (and the Sunday release once public)
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v
uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8   # every hosted practice case, 8 at a time
uv run arena play case:D02 -v                              # the sandbox: 3 demo suppliers, no board
```

**Sunday 08:00:** run `arena data` again - it adds `data/release-sunday` (new news, letters, a
memo). `DataPackage` merges its facts and documents automatically; hidden cases may cite them.

**Master data file:** convert the downloaded package (and an available Sunday release) into one
`master.json` with:

```bash
uv run arena-build-master-data data/package
```

`DataPackage` reads that JSON for lookups, documents, cases and negotiation dossiers. It refreshes
the file automatically when source files change. Its general `query()` method creates a temporary,
read-only in-memory SQLite view from the JSON rows; it does not reopen the source database.

## Hello World (local, 3 commands)

No key yet? Play a whole case against the local simulator - no network, no quota, no LLM costs.
The simulator's supplier is a plain script; the real ones are on arena.tacto.ai. After
`uv sync --all-extras` (step 2 above):

```bash
# terminal 1: the simulator (--data is optional: leave it out until you have run `arena data`)
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package
# terminal 2: a simulator key, then the naive agent plays case:S01
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Hello World" sim                  # prints an api_key
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 ARENA_API_KEY=<the api_key> uv run arena play case:S01 -v
```

It prints the deal, `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the score and a replay link - open it
in your browser: the result on top, then every e-mail of the negotiation.

## Try it by hand (Postman, curl)

Feel the API before you put a model in front of it. On the real arena (practice and sandbox) the
60-second rule applies: three late replies in a row end the thread - too fast for typing. **By
hand, use the simulator first**, without the clock:

```bash
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package           # data/package from `arena data`; --data is optional
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # prints a simulator api_key
export SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8000 KEY=<the api_key>
```

Every call sends `X-API-Key: <key>`; every `POST` also `Content-Type: application/json` and a
fresh `X-Move-Id` (any unique string - the same id again returns the same answer). In Postman:
those headers, the body as raw JSON.

```bash
# 1. the cases: case:S01 has one supplier, sup:70270, and the negotiable fields unit_price, payment_days
curl -s "$SIM/v1/cases?set=practice" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"

# 2. open a session: the reply carries session_id (sim1 on a fresh simulator) and each supplier's quote e-mail
curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Move-Id: open-1" -d '{"case_id": "case:S01"}'

# 3. the supplier's opening e-mail: its term sheet (offer:70270-0) and the quote PDF to fetch
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"

# 4. your e-mail with an offer: the reply is the supplier's answer (status, term_sheets, claim_results)
curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270/messages" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Move-Id: msg-1" \
  -d '{"message": {"subject": "Adapter piece HI", "body": "Thank you for your quote. We offer 15.50 EUR at 60 days.",
       "term_sheets": [{"terms": {"unit_price": 15.5, "payment_days": 60}}]}}'

# 5. read the reply in the thread, and the session state
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

To close, send `{"message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:70270-1"}}}` (the
term sheet you take) or `{"message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}` to the same `messages` path;
the answer carries the result and score. The quote PDF: `GET $SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/attachments/att:70270-0-quote`.
The same calls work on the arena (`https://arena.tacto.ai`, your team's key, a practice case) - with
the clock running.

## The Live Final: waves, in parallel, within the cap

The final comes in 5 themed waves. A wave holds several hidden cases that appear when the host
starts it; play them all in parallel (up to 10 open sessions per key). Each wave has a hard
cap - **8 minutes** (the host may extend one) - and what is still open then ends without a deal.
Start the runner before the first wave and leave it running:

```bash
uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10
```

It polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`, plays every case of a new wave at once (one agent per case),
closes each case **90 seconds before its wave's cap** (read from the wave's `seconds_left`, so an
extension counts) - earlier if a round in that case took longer
(`play.closing_move`: the cheapest standing term
sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats your alternative, else walk away) and stops after the
fifth wave has closed. If it crashes, start it again: it picks up the sessions it had started.
In Python: `play_waves(client, new_agent)`. It reads only your own cases and sessions - during
the final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the screen or the event feed (`arena board`
is for you, not for the agent).

A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute; its time never counts against your 60 seconds,
and the client waits up to 180 seconds for a reply. The client paces itself below the
limit of 10 calls per second and retries dropped connections with the same `X-Move-Id`, so a
retry never sends a message twice. Rehearse with `arena run --set practice --parallel 10` (it counts against your quota) before
Sunday, from the machine and network you will use: every case should end well inside 8 minutes.

## Your own agent

An agent is any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": …, "message": {…}}`.
`threads` holds every e-mail so far per supplier, oldest first; supplier attachments come with
their text under `"text"`. The message is an e-mail - subject, body, up to 3 term sheets - or an
action that closes the case:

```python
from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, complete_offer, play, total_cost
from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
from arena_kit.play import latest, live_threads, standing


class Haggler:
    def decide(self, case, threads):
        sid = live_threads(threads)[0]
        events = threads[sid]
        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)  # the supplier's standing term sheet
        std = standard_terms(events)  # from its quote PDF: what closes if a field is missing
        if latest(events)["status"] in ("agreed", "final_offer"):
            return {
                "supplier_id": sid,
                "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
            }
        ask = complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": terms["unit_price"] * 0.97})
        print("their C:", total_cost(case, terms, std), "ours:", total_cost(case, ask))
        return {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {
                "subject": case["title"],
                "body": "Thank you for your quote. Could you send us a cost breakdown?",
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": ask}],
            },
        }


print(play(RemoteTable(ArenaClient()), "case:P01", Haggler()))
```

| Module | What |
|---|---|
| `client.py` | `ArenaClient`: one method per endpoint (messages, threads, attachments, back office, `me`, ...); paced, safe retries; `practice_remaining` |
| `play.py` | `play()`, `play_all()`, `play_waves()` (the Live Final); `RemoteTable` - the hosted arena (practice, sandbox, final) |
| `cost.py` | the published cost function C with the category goal's rates, `supplier_value` for the relationship term, must-haves, term-sheet completion |
| `docs.py` | supplier documents to text (PDF, XLSX); a quote PDF to its offered, standard and fixed terms |
| `data.py` | the data package and the Sunday release: `facts.json`, read-only SQL, lookup by ID, documents, cases |
| `agents/naive.py` | anchors 10 % low, splits the difference, accepts early - the baseline |
| `agents/llm.py` | the model writes the e-mail and the term sheets from the case and the data it points to; code computes C, reads the documents, removes IDs that do not exist, and refuses bad accepts |
| `sim.py` | `arena-sim`: the public API on your machine, with one plain scripted supplier (below) |
| `mcp_server.py` | the MCP server below |

The LLM agent is a starting point, not a winner: it sees only what the case file points to.
Finding the data that moves a supplier is your job - the worked example below shows one way for
one kind of argument. Ideas beyond it: mine the notes and e-mails, read the suppliers' signals and
documents, send two or three term sheets to learn what a supplier values, ask its roles the right
questions, keep RFQ threads alive in parallel, and never leak urgency, a budget or a missing
alternative.

**Strategic and bottleneck cases** (`category_goal` `stabilise` or `secure_supply`) charge C for a
deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin. Pass your estimate of the supplier to
price it - without one, `total_cost` leaves the term out:

```python
supplier = {"full_cost": 128.0, "interest_rate": 0.12, "standard": std}  # your estimate
total_cost(case, terms, std, supplier)
```

## Worked example: cite an index (case P01)

Brandlhuber, a foundry, announces +9.5 % on volute casings and blames energy and wages. Does the
data agree? `DataPackage` reads the package (the MCP server below gives an LLM the same access):

```python
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

pkg = DataPackage("data/package")
# 1. What drives this part's cost? The category team's estimate:
pkg.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = 'part:310010'")
# -> PPI-C241 (iron and steel) 0.26, PPI-D351 (electric power) 0.06, LCI-C (labour) 0.32
# 2. The letter blames energy: read the electricity producer price index for the last year.
rows = pkg.query(
    "SELECT id, month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-D351' AND month >= '2025-08' ORDER BY month"
)
# 3. Compute the change yourself - two months of one series, at most 12 months apart,
#    ending within the last 12 months of the data.
a, b = rows[0], rows[-1]
change = (b["value"] / a["value"] - 1) * 100
# 4. One sentence: the figure next to both IDs.
print(f"Electricity producer prices changed {change:+.1f}% from {a['month']} to {b['month']} ({a['id']}, {b['id']}).")
# -> Electricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08
#    (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).
```

Put that sentence into your e-mail and read `claim_results` in the reply: `verified` (the figure
matches the data), `irrelevant` (true, but not about this supplier's costs, or the window is too
old) or `contradicted` (a wrong figure - it costs trust). Whether it moves the price, and how far,
is the supplier's business - a true figure may disarm one supplier and leave the next cold; the
replay shows what it made of it. Which series matter to which
supplier, which window, and what else in the data speaks for you - that is up to your agent.

## Choosing a model

`LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` uses the Anthropic SDK (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` talks
to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY`) - OpenAI, Mistral, Groq, a local
Ollama (`http://localhost:11434/v1`) and many more. Or pass your own `complete(system, user) -> str`
to `LLMAgent`. Each message must arrive within **60 seconds** of the supplier's reply: prefer a
fast model or low effort, and do heavy research before you open a session. If the model fails or times out, the agent falls
back to the naive move instead of losing the case.

## Offline: arena-sim, the contract simulator

```bash
uv run arena-sim serve --data /path/to/data/package   # http://127.0.0.1:8000, event code "sim"
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # a simulator key
```

`arena register` exists for the simulator only: it hands out its own keys, which work nowhere
else. The arena's key comes from `/apply` (step 1).

`arena-sim` speaks the arena's public API exactly - paths, fields, statuses, error codes, limits,
the 60-second rule, quote PDFs and cost-breakdown XLSX files in the arena's format, RFQs with
parallel threads, leaderboard and replay JSON - with three example cases (`case:S01`-`S03`). Point
your agent at it to get the plumbing right without a network or a rate limit to worry about.
`--no-clock` switches the 60-second rule off for trying it by hand (above); without it the clock
runs, as on the arena. The first line it prints says which.

Its supplier is a deliberately plain script and **not** how the arena's suppliers behave: it opens
10 % above your current price, concedes a fixed 2 % per term sheet down to 90 %, agrees when you
meet its price, sends a final offer from round 5 and walks if you push after that; cited data is
only checked for existence. **The simulator teaches the contract; the real suppliers think for
themselves** - practise against them in the hosted arena and its sandbox (`--set sandbox`). We
don't hand out our suppliers: for a local opponent, build your own supplier simulator from the
public data - how would a foundry owner with a full order book answer your e-mail?
`starter-kit/Dockerfile` runs the simulator as a container. `uv run pytest` runs the kit's contract
tests against it; set `ARENA_TEST_URL` and `ARENA_TEST_KEY` to run them against a hosted arena too.

## MCP server over the data

A local, read-only MCP server (stdio) lets an MCP-capable agent or chat client explore the data
package itself. Six tools: `list_tables`, `query` (SELECT only, max 200 rows), `lookup` (the fact
behind a citable ID), `list_ids` (e.g. every month of one index series), `read_document`,
`get_case`.

```bash
uv run arena mcp --data /path/to/data/package   # speaks MCP on stdin/stdout
```

Add it to a client, e.g. Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add arena-data -- uv run --directory /path/to/starter-kit arena mcp --data /path/to/data/package
```

or any client with an `mcpServers` config:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"arena-data": {"command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--directory", "/path/to/starter-kit",
  "arena", "mcp", "--data", "/path/to/data/package"]}}}
```

## Good to know

- **60 s per message**, per thread. A late message counts as a timeout (your last offer repeated);
  `play()` reads the supplier's answer and goes on.
- **Invalid messages cost nothing**: `422` and no round used. `409` means the thread or case has
  ended, or you were late.
- **Your key is your team's.** Keep `.env` out of git.
- Tests: `uv run pytest`. Lint: `uv run ruff check .`
